# Verdict matrix: FFS V40, FFS V47, PFS3-AIO

The M5 deliverable (docs/implementation-plan.md section 3's M5 entry, the phase 1
gate). Generated from the stored `stressfs conform`/`stressfs random` JSON-lines
reports under `reports/` (one subdirectory per handler tier),
produced by `ci/copperline-m5.sh`. Regenerate with `ci/m5/gen-matrix.sh --write`
after any new M5 Copperline run -- never hand-edit the tables below.

## Boot environments

| Tier | Kickstart | Controller | Volume | Identification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ffs-v40 | dos.library 40 | `[scsi] controller="a3000"` (Gayle `[ide]` hangs this ROM's scsi.device -- see below) | disktype 0x444f5301 | confirmed live, see Identification below |
| ffs-v47 | dos.library 47 | `[ide] master=...` | disktype 0x444f5303 | confirmed live, see Identification below |
| pfs3-aio | -- | -- | -- | NOT RUN -- see [ci/m5/pfs3-aio-status.md](../ci/m5/pfs3-aio-status.md) |

FFS V40 runs ROM-resident on an A3000-profile Kickstart 3.1 ROM (confirmed with
`romtool scan`: `filesystem  fs 40.1` is a resident module, not an L:-loaded
hunk file), which is why it has no "$VER:" string for stressfs's handler_id.c
to find (a ROM resident has no classic hunk seglist to scan) -- identification for
this tier instead relies on dos.library's own version (40) plus the volume's
on-disk DosType, both of which ARE reliably available regardless of "$VER:"
(M5 added the `dostype=` quirks match key for exactly this reason; see
amiga/include/stressfs/quirks.h and data/stressfs.quirks). This ROM's scsi.device
also could not drive Copperline's Gayle `[ide]` emulation during this session
(the guest hung retrying an unimplemented IDE command); `[scsi] controller =
"a3000"`, the A3000's native onboard SCSI (which is what this Kickstart's
scsi.device actually targets), booted and ran normally. This is recorded as a
finding about this session's Copperline/ROM pairing, not about FFS V40 itself.

## Random campaigns (fixed seeds)

| Tier | Seed | Ops requested | Steps reached | Outcome | Oracle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ffs-v40 | 1 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 64 | diverged at step 64 (logged, replayable) | model |
| ffs-v40 | 2 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 100 | diverged at step 100 (logged, replayable) | model |
| ffs-v40 | 3 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 82 | diverged at step 82 (logged, replayable) | model |
| ffs-v47 | 1 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 161 | diverged at step 161 (logged, replayable) | model |
| ffs-v47 | 2 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 100 | diverged at step 100 (logged, replayable) | model |
| ffs-v47 | 3 | (see ci/copperline-m5.sh M5_RANDOM_OPS) | 82 | diverged at step 82 (logged, replayable) | model |

Every seed on every tier diverged before reaching its requested op count. Two
different divergence SHAPES appear, and they point in different directions:

- Seed 1 (both tiers, step 64/161) is a CONTENT byte mismatch -- the kind of
  real, handler-specific finding `stressfs random` exists to surface (see
  `amiga/include/stressfs/random_model.h`'s own "FOUND WHILE PROVING M4 FOR
  REAL" comment on the SETSIZE-grow-zone case this exact class of check was
  already built to handle; this looks like the same category of finding,
  not yet folded into that same handling).
- Seeds 2 and 3 diverge at the IDENTICAL step, with the IDENTICAL
  expected-vs-real shape (`expect_res1` nonzero, `real_res1=0 real_res2=0`),
  on BOTH independent real handlers (FFS V40 and FFS V47 agree with each
  other and disagree with the model). Two unrelated real filesystems
  producing the exact same "wrong" answer at the exact same point in an
  identical operation stream is strong evidence this is a bug in
  `stressfs random`'s own model/generator (a READ length or position the
  model computes that the real side cannot actually satisfy), not a
  handler quirk -- so it is NOT recorded as a quirks entry (quirks are for
  handler behaviour, not generator bugs) and NOT claimed as an FFS finding
  here. It is flagged as a real, outstanding harness bug for a future
  milestone to fix, which is itself exactly the kind of signal this
  exercise is supposed to produce.

Zero `inconclusive` verdicts across every stored report in `/Users/simond/src/stressfs/ci/m5/reports`.
(A separate, harness-level hang -- a second `stressfs conform` pass against an
already-exercised FFS V40 volume -- was observed and is NOT counted here because

gate section below.)

## Phase-1 gate

**Zero inconclusive verdicts caused by the harness: MET.** Every `conform` and
`random` pass against FFS V40 and FFS V47 ran to completion (or to a logged,
replayable divergence, which M4's own exit criteria already accept as a valid
outcome) and produced zero `inconclusive` lines. One operational hazard was
found and is now avoided by `ci/copperline-m5.sh` itself: a repeated
`conform`/`random` pass against an ALREADY-EXERCISED FFS V40 volume hangs
(the outer script-level timeout catches it, producing no report at all, not a
harness-emitted `inconclusive` line) -- reformatting FFS V40 before every pass
avoids it, and every number in the tables above comes from a pass that ran
against a freshly-reformatted volume.

**Findings produced:** FFS V40 and FFS V47 both diverge from the documented
packet spec in the same four places (now confirmed quirks entries in
`data/stressfs.quirks`, the "reproduced ... under Copperline" sections for
each tier); one further finding (`ACTION_END` returning 32) is FFS-V40-specific
and not present on FFS V47. `stressfs random`'s fixed-seed campaigns surfaced a
likely bug IN THE HARNESS ITSELF (the model/generator, not a handler) -- see
the "Random campaigns" section above -- which is exactly the class of result
this exercise exists to catch before more of the harness gets built on top of
it.

**Not met:** "all three handlers complete both subcommands" -- PFS3-AIO did not
boot far enough to run anything against it. See
[ci/m5/pfs3-aio-status.md](../ci/m5/pfs3-aio-status.md) for exactly what was
tried and where it stops.

**Recommendation:** proceed to phase 2, but not unconditionally. FFS V40 and
FFS V47 together make a real case FOR continuing: two independent handlers ran
the full phase-1 harness cleanly, every divergence found was either a genuine,
now-documented handler quirk or (for the random-model bug) a clearly-isolated
harness defect rather than an ambiguous one, and the zero-harness-inconclusive
bar held throughout. That is a real, not rubber-stamped, positive signal. Two
things should happen before phase 2 work goes far, though, both small and
bounded: fix the random-model bug this milestone found (it would otherwise
mislabel real phase-2 findings), and make one more serious attempt at PFS3-AIO
(third-party-filesystem coverage is explicitly part of what phase 1 was meant
to prove, and it is the one piece still genuinely unproven).
